problems.stem: Your slide has a chart showing club membership rising from 20 to 55. Which alt text is most useful to a screen reader user?
options: Bar chart showing club membership rising from 20 members in fall to 55 in spring.
problems.explanation: Good alt text describes what the image shows and why it matters. A filename or the word 'image' tells the reader nothing.

problems.stem: You want section titles in your document. You make each line 20pt bold so it looks like a heading. Why can this fail an accessibility check?
options: Bold text is too hard to read on screens.
Screen readers and document navigation rely on real heading styles or tags, not on visual size, so bold-only titles are not recognized as headings.
Headings must always be underlined, not bold.
20pt is too small for any heading.
problems.explanation: Use real heading styles (Heading 1, Heading 2) or tags (h1, h2). Visual size alone does not create the structure assistive tools depend on.

problems.stem: You ask an AI tool to generate alt text for a complex diagram and it returns one vague line: "A diagram about a process." How should you use this output responsibly?
options: Use it as-is; AI alt text is always compliant.
Treat it as a draft, then rewrite it to name the actual steps shown, because you are responsible for whether the alt text is accurate.
Delete the diagram so you do not need alt text.
Ask the AI to make the alt text longer without checking accuracy.
problems.explanation: AI-generated alt text is a starting point. You must verify it describes the real content; vague output does not meet the need.

problems.stem: A form marks required fields only by coloring their labels red. Why might this exclude some users, and what is the fix?
options: Red is unprofessional; change it to blue.
Users who cannot distinguish red cannot tell which fields are required; add a text label or asterisk such as "Required" so meaning does not depend on color alone.
There is no problem if the red is bright enough.
Remove the colors and leave the fields unmarked.
problems.explanation: Color alone can hide meaning from users who cannot distinguish it. Pair color with text or an icon so the cue is reliable.
